overall: The AG found the School Committee Chair violated the Open Meeting Law by emailing a quorum of the Committee on public business, but found no violation by the Committee as a whole; the email exchange must be disclosed publicly.

allegations.summary: The Committee Chair allegedly emailed a quorum of the School Committee, replying to all recipients, on a public business matter (renaming the winter break).
allegations.key_passage: It was therefore improper for the Chair to copy her fellow committee members on this email.

allegations.summary: Whether the Committee as a whole violated the law through the Chair's email, given that the other members copied did not respond.
allegations.key_passage: because the other Committee members did not respond to the e-mail, we find that the Committee as a whole did not violate the law.

remedy: Publicly disclose the September 18, 2014 email exchange, if not already done, at the Committee's next meeting.
remedy_passage: Additionally, we order the Committee to publicly disclose the September 18, 2014 email exchange, if it has not done so already, at its next meeting.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
